resources.title: Can we find the turning points on the curve $y = \sin x + \cos x$?
resources.evidence: turning points of y = sin x + cos x on (0, 2pi) via dy/dx = cos x - sin x = 0 - the canonical 3.4.1 use of the standard derivatives, with the R-form of 3.3.2 as the recorded alternative (flips the lane-11 non-overlap row of record routed 'P3 3.4 Differentiation')

resources.title: What happens when we differentiate $\sin^4x + 2 \cos^2x - \cos^4x$?
resources.evidence: chain rule on sin^4 x, cos^2 x, cos^4 x gives d/dx = 0 identically - the expression is the constant 1; the deduction task on the 3.4.1 composite derivatives

resources.title: Can we find the velocity and acceleration of this particle?
resources.evidence: v = ds/dt and a = dv/dt for s = 12 sin(3t/2) - the 3.4.1 composite derivative of sin(3t/2) by the chain rule is the load-bearing computation (mechanics clothing); the remaining parts are 1.5 trig equations

resources.title: Can we find a tangent to $y=1/(1+x^2)$?
resources.evidence: gradient of y = 1/(1+x^2) via the chain rule on (1+x^2)^-1 giving -2x/(1+x^2)^2, then the tangent-line condition from (0,1) - the derivative work is load-bearing; the pi>3 coda is an area argument (3.5 bearing)

resources.title: Trig gradient match
resources.evidence: pairing trig functions with their gradient functions incl. the scaled composites - builds d/dx(sin x) = cos x and the chain-rule cases graphically; excerpt-capture disclosure: no solution well of record, matched on the provider task statement

resources.title: Powerful derivatives
resources.evidence: prove d/dx x^a = a x^(a-1) for real a by writing x^a = e^(a ln x) and chaining the standard derivatives - the ln/exponential derivative law of 3.4.1 is the engine (flips the lane-10 non-overlap row of record routed 'P3 3.4 Differentiation')

resources.title: Can you find... chain rule edition
resources.evidence: working backwards from conditions on f(g(x)) (stationary points at prescribed x, a local minimum of ln g(x), no stationary points) - chain-rule composition reasoning with the 3.4.1 list as the toolset (flips the lane-10 non-overlap row of record routed 'P3 3.4 Differentiation')

resources.title: Can we show $x>\ln(1+x^2)$ for all $x>0$?
resources.evidence: d/dx (x - ln(1+x^2)) = 1 - 2x/(1+x^2) >= 0 by the 3.4.1 composite derivative of ln(1+x^2), deducing x > ln(1+x^2) for x > 0 - the increasing-function argument (flips the lane-10 non-overlap row of record routed 'P3 3.4 Differentiation')

resources.title: Which is the greater of $e^{\pi}$ and $\pi^e$?
resources.evidence: stationary point of x^(1/x) via d/dx(ln y) = (1 - ln x)/x^2 - ln/composite 3.4.1 work deciding e^pi > pi^e without a calculator (flips the lane-10 non-overlap row of record routed 'P3 3.4 Differentiation')

resources.title: Can we sketch $y=3 \cos x - \cos 3x$?
resources.evidence: d/dx (3 cos x - cos 3x) = 6 sin x cos 2x proved by the chain rule on cos 3x plus the product-to-sum identity, then the increasing ranges and the sketch (flips the lane-11 non-overlap row of record routed 'P3 3.4 Differentiation')

resources.title: Rotating derivatives
resources.evidence: the unit-circle velocity vector (-sin t, cos t) assembled from the rotating diagrams - the geometric derivation of d/dt(sin t) = cos t and d/dt(cos t) = -sin t, the 3.4.1 standard facts (flips the lane-11 non-overlap row of record routed 'P3 3.4 Differentiation')

resources.title: Similar derivatives
resources.evidence: d(tan theta)/dtheta via similar triangles with vertices (1, tan theta) and (cot theta, 1) - in-spec for the tan limb of 3.4.1; the sec/cot extensions are beyond the 3.4.1 list and are disclosed (flips the lane-11 non-overlap row of record routed 'P3 3.4 Differentiation')

resources.title: Sine stretching

resources.title: Can we differentiate $e^{2x}( 2 \cos (3x) + 3 \sin (3x))$?
resources.evidence: d/dx of e^(2x)(2 cos 3x + 3 sin 3x) by the product rule with the 3.4.1 composite derivatives inside - the exact CIE product-rule-plus-standard-derivatives showcase (flips the lane-10 non-overlap row of record routed 'P3 3.4 Differentiation')

resources.title: How does your rectangle grow?
resources.evidence: the fixed-height rectangle argument dA/dt = v du/dt extended to both sides varying - the visual derivation of the product rule d(uv)/dt = v du/dt + u dv/dt, the 3.4.2 law itself

resources.title: Can we sketch $y=x^2/(1+x^4)$?
resources.evidence: turning points of y = x^2/(1+x^4) via the product rule on x^2 (1+x^4)^-1 giving dy/dx = 2x(1-x^4)/(1+x^4)^2 - stationary points at 0, +/-1 and the sketch

resources.title: Can we sketch the curve $y=1/((x-a)^2-1)$?
resources.evidence: stationary points of g(x) = 1/(((x-a)^2-1)((x-b)^2-1)) found by differentiating the product of reciprocal quadratics - the product/quotient-rule work is load-bearing for the three stationary abscissae

resources.title: Can we sketch the graph of $y=x(x+1)(x-2)^4$?
resources.evidence: gradient of y = x(x+1)(x-2)^4 shown as (x-2)^3(6x^2+x-2) by the product rule, all stationary points with nature, then the y^2 and even-power variant sketches

resources.title: Can we find this body's displacement from $O$ when its velocity is $0$?
resources.evidence: acceleration as d/dt of v = (2t-1)/(4(2t+1)) by the quotient rule (a = 1/(2t+2)^2) - the quotient-rule computation is the tested skill in kinematics clothing; the displacement part is an integral (3.5 bearing)

resources.title: Can we show the function $(2x+1)/(x^2-1)$ can take all real values?
resources.evidence: f'(x) = -2(x^2+x+1)/(x^2-1)^2 by the quotient rule, always negative, with the inflection argued from the behaviour of f' between the asymptotes - the range part is the recorded discriminant method

resources.title: Which values can $x(x-3)/(x-4)$ take?
resources.evidence: the range of y = x(x-3)/(x-4) shown both by the discriminant and by the quotient rule (both approaches of record) - stationary points at the range endpoints; the 5/x comparison is algebraic

resources.title: Given that $y = (x+6)^7(x-9)^8$, can we find $dy/dx$?
resources.evidence: dy/dx of y = (x+6)^7 (x-9)^8 by the product rule and the zeros of dy/dx - the canonical 3.4.2 product-rule exercise

resources.title: Where are the stationary points on $\cot x-8\cos x$?

resources.title: Can we sketch the curve $y=e^{-x}/(1+x^2)$?

resources.title: Can we sketch the curve $y=(x-a)e^x/(x-b)$?

resources.title: Can we find the equation of the normal to the curve when $t = 2$?

resources.title: Implicit circles

resources.title: How many normals to a parabola pass through $P$?

resources.title: What can we say if a normal to an ellipse passes through this point?

resources.title: What can we say if this hyperbola and parabola meet at right angles?

resources.title: Can we find the angle between these two tangents?

resources.title: Can we show that these normals meet on the $x$-axis?

resources.title: What can we say if a point $P$ on an ellipse is directly above the focus?

resources.title: Can we show this parabola and this ellipse meet at right angles?

resources.title: Can we show these tangents to this hyperbola form a square?

resources.title: Where does this tangent to this ellipse meet $x=a$?

resources.title: When do these normals to a parabola meet on the parabola?
